NKJV.1: Woe to you who are at ease in Zion, And trust in Mount Samaria, Notable persons in the chief nation, To whom the house of Israel comes!
NKJV.2: Go over to Calneh and see; And from there go to Hamath the great; Then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Or is their territory greater than your territory?
NKJV.3: Woe to you who put far off the day of doom, Who cause the seat of violence to come near;
NKJV.4: Who lie on beds of ivory, Stretch out on your couches, Eat lambs from the flock And calves from the midst of the stall;
NKJV.5: Who sing idly to the sound of stringed instruments, And invent for yourselves musical instruments like David;
NKJV.6: Who drink wine from bowls, And anoint yourselves with the best ointments,  But are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.
NKJV.7: Therefore they shall now go captive as the first of the captives, And those who recline at banquets shall be removed.
NKJV.8: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself, The LORD God of hosts says: “I abhor the pride of Jacob, And hate his palaces; Therefore I will deliver up the city And all that is in it.”
NKJV.9: Then it shall come to pass, that if ten men remain in one house, they shall die.
NKJV.10: And when a relative of the dead, with one who will burn the bodies, picks up the bodies to take them out of the house, he will say to one inside the house, “Are there any more with you?” Then someone will say, “None.” And he will say, “Hold your tongue! For we dare not mention the name of the LORD.”
NKJV.11: For behold, the LORD gives a command:  He will break the great house into bits, And the little house into pieces.
NKJV.12: Do horses run on rocks? Does one plow there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into gall, And the fruit of righteousness into wormwood,
NKJV.13: You who rejoice over Lo Debar, Who say, “Have we not taken Karnaim for ourselves By our own strength?”
NKJV.14: “But, behold, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel,” Says the LORD God of hosts; “And they will afflict you from the entrance of Hamath To the Valley of the Arabah.”

ESV.1: “Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
ESV.2: Pass over to Calneh, and see, and from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Or is their territory greater than your territory,
ESV.3: O you who put far away the day of disaster and bring near the seat of violence?
ESV.4: “Woe to those who lie on beds of ivory and stretch themselves out on their couches, and eat lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall,
ESV.5: who sing idle songs to the sound of the harp and like David invent for themselves instruments of music,
ESV.6: who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph!
ESV.7: Therefore they shall now be the first of those who go into exile, and the revelry of those who stretch themselves out shall pass away.”
ESV.8: The Lord GOD has sworn by himself, declares the LORD, the God of hosts: “I abhor the pride of Jacob and hate his strongholds, and I will deliver up the city and all that is in it.”
ESV.9: And if ten men remain in one house, they shall die.
ESV.10: And when one's relative, the one who anoints him for burial, shall take him up to bring the bones out of the house, and shall say to him who is in the innermost parts of the house, “Is there still anyone with you?” he shall say, “No”; and he shall say, “Silence! We must not mention the name of the LORD.”
ESV.11: For behold, the LORD commands, and the great house shall be struck down into fragments, and the little house into bits.
ESV.12: Do horses run on rocks? Does one plow there  with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood  —
ESV.13: you who rejoice in Lo-debar,  who say, “Have we not by our own strength captured Karnaim  for ourselves?”
ESV.14: “For behold, I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD, the God of hosts; “and they shall oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.”

NASB.1: Woe to those who are at ease in Zion And to those who [feel] secure in the mountain of Samaria, The distinguished men of the foremost of nations, To whom the house of Israel comes.
NASB.2: Go over to Calneh and look, And go from there to Hamath the great, Then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms, Or is their territory greater than yours?
NASB.3: Do you put off the day of calamity, And would you bring near the seat of violence?
NASB.4: Those who recline on beds of ivory And sprawl on their couches, And eat lambs from the flock And calves from the midst of the stall,
NASB.5: Who improvise to the sound of the harp, [And] like David have composed songs for themselves,
NASB.6: Who drink wine from sacrificial bowls While they anoint themselves with the finest of oils, Yet they have not grieved over the ruin of Joseph.
NASB.7: Therefore, they will now go into exile at the head of the exiles, And the sprawlers' banqueting will pass away.
NASB.8: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself, the LORD God of hosts has declared: 'I loathe the arrogance of Jacob, And detest his citadels; Therefore I will deliver up [the] city and all it contains.'
NASB.9: And it will be, if ten men are left in one house, they will die.
NASB.10: Then one's uncle, or his undertaker, will lift him up to carry out [his] bones from the house, and he will say to the one who is in the innermost part of the house, 'Is anyone else with you?' And that one will say, 'No one.' Then he will answer, 'Keep quiet. For the name of the LORD is not to be mentioned.'
NASB.11: For behold, the LORD is going to command that the great house be smashed to pieces and the small house to fragments.
NASB.12: Do horses run on rocks? Or does one plow them with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison And the fruit of righteousness into wormwood,
NASB.13: You who rejoice in Lodebar, And say, 'Have we not by our [own] strength taken Karnaim for ourselves?'
NASB.14: 'For behold, I am going to raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel,' declares the LORD God of hosts, 'And they will afflict you from the entrance of Hamath To the brook of the Arabah.'

NLT.1:
What sorrow awaits you who lounge in luxury in Jerusalem,
and you who feel secure in Samaria!
You are famous and popular in Israel,
and people go to you for help.
NLT.2:
But go over to Calneh
and see what happened there.
Then go to the great city of Hamath
and down to the Philistine city of Gath.
You are no better than they were,
and look at how they were destroyed.
NLT.3:
You push away every thought of coming disaster,
but your actions only bring the day of judgment closer.
NLT.4:
How terrible for you who sprawl on ivory beds
and lounge on your couches,
eating the meat of tender lambs from the flock
and of choice calves fattened in the stall.
NLT.5:
You sing trivial songs to the sound of the harp
and fancy yourselves to be great musicians like David.
NLT.6:
You drink wine by the bowlful
and perfume yourselves with fragrant lotions.
You care nothing about the ruin of your nation.
NLT.7:
Therefore, you will be the first to be led away as captives.
Suddenly, all your parties will end.
NLT.8:
The Sovereign LORD has sworn by his own name, and this is what he, the LORD God of Heaven’s Armies, says: “I despise the arrogance of Israel,
and I hate their fortresses.
I will give this city
and everything in it to their enemies.”
NLT.9: (If there are ten men left in one house, they will all die.
NLT.10: And when a relative who is responsible to dispose of the dead goes into the house to carry out the bodies, he will ask the last survivor, “Is anyone else with you?” When the person begins to swear, “No, by . . . ,” he will interrupt and say, “Stop! Don’t even mention the name of the LORD.”)
NLT.11:
When the LORD gives the command,
homes both great and small will be smashed to pieces.
NLT.12:
Can horses gallop over boulders?
Can oxen be used to plow them?
But that’s how foolish you are when you turn justice into poison
and the sweet fruit of righteousness into bitterness.
NLT.13:
And you brag about your conquest of Lo-debar.
You boast, “Didn’t we take Karnaim by our own strength?”
NLT.14:
“O people of Israel, I am about to bring an enemy nation against you,”
says the LORD God of Heaven’s Armies.
“They will oppress you throughout your land —
from Lebo-hamath in the north
to the Arabah Valley in the south.”

WEB.1: Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who are secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel come!
WEB.2: Go to Calneh, and see; and from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. are they better than these kingdoms? or is their border greater than your border?
WEB.3: Those who put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence to come near;
WEB.4: Who lie on beds of ivory, and stretch themselves on their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the middle of the stall;
WEB.5: who strum on the strings of a harp; who invent for themselves instruments of music, like David;
WEB.6: who drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best oils; but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.
WEB.7: Therefore they will now go captive with the first who go captive; and the feasting and lounging will end.
WEB.8: “The Lord Yahweh has sworn by himself,” says Yahweh, the God of Armies: “I abhor the pride of Jacob, and detest his fortresses. Therefore I will deliver up the city with all that is in it.
WEB.9: It will happen, if there remain ten men in one house, that they shall die.
WEB.10: “When a man’s relative carries him, even he who burns him, to bring bodies out of the house, and asks him who is in the innermost parts of the house, ‘Is there yet any with you?’ And he says, ‘No;’ then he will say, ‘Hush! Indeed we must not mention Yahweh’s name.’
WEB.11: “For, behold, Yahweh commands, and the great house will be smashed to pieces, and the little house into bits.
WEB.12: Do horses run on the rocky crags? Does one plow there with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness;
WEB.13: you who rejoice in a thing of nothing, who say, ‘Haven’t we taken for ourselves horns by our own strength?’
WEB.14: For, behold, I will raise up against you a nation, house of Israel,” says Yahweh, the God of Armies; “and they will afflict you from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of the Arabah.”

AMP.1:
Woe (judgment is coming) to those who are at ease and carefree in Zion (Judah)
And to those on the mountain of Samaria who feel secure,
The distinguished men of the foremost of nations,
To whom the house of Israel comes.
AMP.2:
Go over to Calneh [in Babylonia] and look,
And from there go [north of Damascus] to the great city of Hamath;
Then go down to Gath of the Philistines.
Are they better than these kingdoms [of yours],
Or is their territory greater than yours?
AMP.3:
Do you put off the day of punishment,
Yet cause the seat of violence to come near?
AMP.4:
Those who lie on [luxurious] beds of ivory
And lounge around out on their couches,
And eat lambs from the flock
And calves from the midst of the stall,
AMP.5:
Who improvise to the sound of the harp—
Like David they have composed songs for themselves—
AMP.6:
Who drink wine from sacrificial bowls
And anoint themselves with the finest oils [reflecting their unrestrained celebration];
Yet they are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph (Israel).
AMP.7:
Therefore, they will now go into exile with the first of the captives,
And the cultic revelry and banqueting of those who lounge around [on their luxurious couches] will pass away.
AMP.8:
The Lord GOD has sworn [an oath] by Himself—the LORD God of hosts, says:
"I loathe and reject the [self-centered] arrogance of Jacob (Israel),
And I hate his palaces and citadels;
Therefore, I shall hand over the [idolatrous] city [of Samaria] with all that it contains [to the Assyrian invaders]."
AMP.9: And it shall come to pass that if there remain ten men in one house, they shall die [by the pestilence that comes with war].
AMP.10: Then one's uncle, or his undertaker, shall come to bring the [disease-infected] body out of the house, [to cremate it], and he will say to another in the farthest part of the house, "Is there anyone else with you?" And that one will say, "No one." Then he will respond, "Hush! Keep quiet! For the name of the LORD is not to be mentioned [even casually, for fear that we might invoke even more punishment]."
AMP.11: For behold, the LORD is going to command that the great house be smashed to pieces and the small house to fragments.
AMP.12:
Do horses run on rocks?
Do men plow rocks with oxen? [Of course not!]
Yet you have turned justice into poison
And the fruit of righteousness into wormwood (bitterness),
AMP.13:
You who [self-confidently] rejoice in Lo-debar (Nothing),
Who say, "Have we not by our own strength taken Karnaim (Strength) for ourselves?"
AMP.14:
"For behold, I am going to stir up a nation against you,
O house of Israel," says the LORD, the God of hosts,
"And they will afflict and torment you [to the entire limits of Israel] from the entrance of Hamath [in the north]
To the brook of the Arabah [in the south]."

MSG.1:
Woe to you who think you live on easy street in Zion,
who think Mount Samaria is the good life.
You assume you're at the top of the heap,
voted the number-one best place to live.
MSG.2:
Well, wake up and look around. Get off your pedestal.
Take a look at Calneh.
Go and visit Great Hamath.
Look in on Gath of the Philistines.
Doesn't that take you off your high horse?
Compared to them, you're not much, are you?
MSG.3:
Woe to you who are rushing headlong to disaster!
Catastrophe is just around the corner!
MSG.4:
Woe to those who live in luxury
and expect everyone else to serve them!
MSG.5:
Woe to those who live only for today,
indifferent to the fate of others!
Woe to the playboys, the playgirls,
who think life is a party held just for them!
MSG.6:
Woe to those addicted to feeling good—life without pain!
those obsessed with looking good—life without wrinkles!
They could not care less
about their country going to ruin.
MSG.7:
But here's what's really coming:
a forced march into exile.
They'll leave the country whining,
a rag-tag bunch of good-for-nothings.
MSG.8:
God, the Master, has sworn, and solemnly stands by his Word.
The God-of-the-Angel-Armies speaks:
"I hate the arrogance of Jacob.
I have nothing but contempt for his forts.
I'm about to hand over the city
and everyone in it."
MSG.9: Ten men are in a house, all dead.
MSG.10: A relative comes and gets the bodies to prepare them for a decent burial. He discovers a survivor huddled in a closet and asks, "Are there any more?" The answer: "Not a soul. But hush! God must not be mentioned in this desecrated place."
MSG.11:
Note well: God issues the orders.
He'll knock large houses to smithereens.
He'll smash little houses to bits.
MSG.12:
Do you hold a horse race in a field of rocks?
Do you plow the sea with oxen?
You'd cripple the horses
and drown the oxen.
And yet you've made a shambles of justice,
a bloated corpse of righteousness,
MSG.13:
Bragging of your trivial pursuits,
beating up on the weak and crowing, "Look what I've done!"
MSG.14:
"Enjoy it while you can, you Israelites.
I've got a pagan army on the move against you"
—this is your God speaking, God-of-the-Angel-Armies—
"And they'll make hash of you,
from one end of the country to the other."

NIV.1:
Woe to the Complacent

and to you who feel secure on Mount Samaria,
you notable men of the foremost nation,
to whom the people of Israel come!
NIV.2:
Go to Calneh and look at it;
go from there to great Hamath,
and then go down to Gath in Philistia.
Are they better off than your two kingdoms?
Is their land larger than yours?

and bring near a reign of terror.

and lounge on your couches.

and fattened calves.
NIV.5:
You strum away on your harps like David
and improvise on musical instruments.
NIV.6:
You drink wine by the bowlful
and use the finest lotions,
but you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
NIV.7:
Therefore you will be among the first to go into exile;
your feasting and lounging will end.
NIV.8:
The Lord Abhors the Pride of Israel
The Sovereign Lord has sworn by himself—the Lord God Almighty declares:
“I abhor the pride of Jacob
and detest his fortresses;
I will deliver up the city
and everything in it.”
NIV.9: If ten men are left in one house, they too will die.
NIV.10: And if a relative who is to burn the bodies comes to carry them out of the house and asks anyone still hiding there, “Is anyone with you?” and he says, “No,” then he will say, “Hush! We must not mention the name of the Lord.”
NIV.11:
For the Lord has given the command,
and he will smash the great house into pieces
and the small house into bits.
NIV.12:
Do horses run on the rocky crags?
Does one plow there with oxen?
But you have turned justice into poison
and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness—
NIV.13:
you who rejoice in the conquest of Lo Debar
and say, “Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?”
NIV.14:
For the Lord God Almighty declares,
“I will stir up a nation against you, O house of Israel,
that will oppress you all the way
from Lebo Hamath to the valley of the Arabah.”

NET.1: Woe to those who live in ease in Zion, to those who feel secure on Mount Samaria. They think of themselves as the elite class of the best nation. The family of Israel looks to them for leadership.
NET.2: They say to the people: “Journey over to Calneh and look at it! Then go from there to Hamath-Rabbah! Then go down to Gath of the Philistines! Are they superior to our two kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?”
NET.3: You refuse to believe a day of disaster will come, but you establish a reign of violence.
NET.4: They lie around on beds decorated with ivory, and sprawl out on their couches. They eat lambs from the flock, and calves from the middle of the pen.
NET.5: They sing to the tune of stringed instruments; like David they invent musical instruments.
NET.6: They drink wine from sacrificial bowls, and pour the very best oils on themselves. Yet they are not concerned over the ruin of Joseph.
NET.7: Therefore they will now be the first to go into exile, and the religious banquets where they sprawl on couches will end.
NET.8: The sovereign LORD confirms this oath by his very own life. The LORD, the God who commands armies, is speaking: “I despise Jacob’s arrogance; I hate their fortresses. I will hand over to their enemies the city of Samaria and everything in it.”
NET.9: If ten men are left in one house, they too will die.
NET.10: When their close relatives, the ones who will burn the corpses, pick up their bodies to remove the bones from the house, they will say to anyone who is in the inner rooms of the house, “Is anyone else with you?” He will respond, “Be quiet! Don’t invoke the LORD’s name!”
NET.11: Indeed, look! The LORD is giving the command. He will smash the large house to bits, and the small house into little pieces.
NET.12: Can horses run on rocky cliffs? Can one plow the sea with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into a poisonous plant, and the fruit of righteous actions into a bitter plant.
NET.13: You are happy because you conquered Lo-Debar. You say, “Did we not conquer Karnaim by our own power?”
NET.14: “Look! I am about to bring a nation against you, family of Israel.” The LORD, the God who commands armies, is speaking. “They will oppress you all the way from Lebo-Hamath to the Stream of the Arabah.”
